questions.q: What is the minimum age to vote in India?
questions.explanation: The Constitution of India (Article 326) sets the minimum voting age at 18. Reduced from 21 by the 61st Amendment Act, 1988.

questions.q: Which document is the primary proof of identity for voting?
questions.explanation: The EPIC (Voter ID Card) is the primary identity document issued by the Election Commission.

questions.q: What is Form 6 used for?
questions.explanation: Form 6 is for inclusion of name in the electoral roll — used by new voters to register.

questions.q: How can you check if your name is on the voter list?
questions.explanation: The NVSP (voters.eci.gov.in) lets citizens search the electoral roll using EPIC number or personal details.

questions.q: Can NRIs vote in Indian elections?
options: Yes, in person at registered constituency
questions.explanation: NRIs can vote but must be present in person at their registered polling station per the 2010 Amendment Act.

questions.q: What does EVM stand for?
questions.explanation: EVM = Electronic Voting Machine. India began using EVMs in 1982 and they became universal by 2004.

questions.q: What is VVPAT?
questions.explanation: VVPAT prints a slip showing the candidate voted for, allowing voter verification.

questions.q: What is the 'NOTA' option?
questions.explanation: NOTA allows voters to officially reject all candidates. Introduced by the Supreme Court in 2013.

questions.q: Why is indelible ink applied during voting?
options: Track who voted for which party
questions.explanation: Indelible ink prevents the same person from voting twice. It contains silver nitrate and lasts several days.

questions.q: What is the 'silence period' before elections?
questions.explanation: Campaigning must stop 48 hours before polling to let voters decide without last-minute influence.

questions.q: Minimum age to contest Lok Sabha elections?
questions.explanation: Must be 25 years old per Article 84 of the Indian Constitution.

questions.q: Security deposit for filing nomination?
questions.explanation: ₹25,000 (₹12,500 for SC/ST). Forfeited if candidate fails to secure 1/6th of valid votes.

questions.q: What is the Model Code of Conduct?
questions.explanation: MCC is guidelines issued by the Election Commission governing behavior of parties, candidates, and government during elections.

questions.q: Can a person contest from multiple constituencies?
questions.explanation: A candidate can contest from max two constituencies. If elected from both, must vacate one within 14 days.

questions.q: Who is the Returning Officer?
questions.explanation: The RO manages elections in a constituency — accepting nominations, overseeing polling, declaring results.

questions.q: India's electoral system for Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: India uses FPTP — candidate with most votes wins, regardless of absolute majority.

questions.q: Seats needed for Lok Sabha majority?
questions.explanation: Lok Sabha has 543 seats. Majority = 272 (50%+1).

questions.q: What if no party gets clear majority?
questions.explanation: A 'hung parliament' leads to coalition formation. President invites largest party/coalition to prove majority.

questions.q: Days to challenge election results?
questions.explanation: Election petition must be filed in High Court within 45 days per the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

questions.q: What are postal ballots for?
options: Voting by those who can't visit stations
questions.explanation: Postal ballots allow service voters, disabled persons, and senior citizens (80+) to vote by mail.

questions.q: Which body conducts elections in India?
questions.explanation: The ECI is an autonomous constitutional body under Article 324 responsible for all elections.

questions.q: How often are Lok Sabha elections?
questions.explanation: Every 5 years unless dissolved earlier. Term is 5 years from first meeting.

questions.q: What is a constituency?
questions.explanation: A constituency is a defined area whose residents elect a representative. India has 543 Lok Sabha constituencies.

questions.q: What is 'universal adult suffrage'?
questions.explanation: Every citizen 18+ can vote regardless of race, gender, religion, or income. India adopted this from its first election in 1951-52.

questions.q: What is an exit poll?
options: Survey of voters after casting vote
Poll to decide if elections happen
questions.explanation: Exit polls survey voters after voting. Cannot be broadcast until the last voting phase concludes.
